record.name: Svetlana Sabo
record.title: Full Professor
record.department: Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics)
record.bio: Svetlana Sabo received her Diploma Engineer degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 1998 and her PhD from the same institution in 2005, with a thesis on moisture transport across elastomeric seals in low-pressure enclosures. She joined the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences as an Assistant Professor in 2006 and was promoted to Full Professor in 2018. Her research group focuses on thermal-fluid behaviour inside sealed cavities, with particular emphasis on hygrothermal modelling, condensation onset prediction, and the influence of seal geometry and vapour permeability on internal dew-point conditions. She teaches courses in fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and machine elements. The group operates a climate-controlled test chamber, a gravimetric vapour sorption analyser, and a suite of infrared thermography equipment.
open_to: consulting on enclosure design for moisture control
joint projects on material characterisation or hygrothermal simulation
student internships in experimental thermal-fluid measurement
equipment access (climate chamber, gravimetric vapour sorption analyser, infrared thermography)
record.industry_experience: Sabo provided a six-month consulting engagement to a domestic manufacturer of outdoor metering cabinets, advising on gasket material selection and anti-condensation heater sizing. She has also contributed expert opinion in two product certification disputes concerning moisture ingress in sealed outdoor housings.
record.notes: Sabo has a preference for collaborations that involve real hardware and field validation rather than purely simulation-based studies. Her laboratory has limited availability in the autumn semester due to teaching load; project kick-off meetings and intensive measurement campaigns are better scheduled in spring or summer.
